correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the 7-edge ladder, its 14 incidence-orientations as primitive vectors, and all compatible acyclic directed forests; enumeration by 14-bit masks and 3^7 edge states yields 575 nonempty faces, f=(14,74,184,213,90). Deterministic 14-stage toggle order gives 285 distinct valid face-poset pairs; all 2002 Hasse covers oriented with matched arrows reversed form a DAG. Exactly one critical 0-cell, two critical 3-cells and two critical 4-cells remain. Independently evaluated exact signed gradient-path reduction, obtaining integral 4→3 Morse matrix [[0,0],[0,0]]. Since π3(S³∨S³)≅H3(S³∨S³;Z)=Z² by Hurewicz, both dimension-four attaching maps are null; hence the full claimed mixed-dimensional wedge. This goes beyond mod-p Betti ranks.

value.rationale: The 3-rung ladder is the first noncycle/non-tree Cartesian ladder after C4, a natural small graph family member with 2 independent cycles. Its ordinary Morse complex has an uncommon mixture of sphere dimensions; an exact integral attaching-map computation distinguishes homotopy from numerical homology and gives a reusable base case for ladder/directed-forest topology. A single exact natural graph invariant is worthwhile without an all-ladder theorem.

final_claim: For the ordinary discrete-vector-field Morse complex of the three-rung ladder graph L3=P3□K2, the integral homotopy type is ∨²S³∨∨²S⁴.
limitations: Single ordinary graph Morse complex of L3 only, no all-size ladder result.
Finite integer computation establishes the exact L3 homotopy type but is not a formal Lean proof or external expert attestation.
